newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-UNBEATEN PARIS SG FACE HARD TASK IN LYON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNBEATEN PARIS SG FACE HARD TASK IN LYON.

text.p: French league leaders Paris St Germain start to feel the pressure of a tight schedule as they travel to in-form Lyon on Wednesday.
The Parisians, in the lead on 21 points, three points ahead of Bastia, were lucky to get away with a 2-2 draw at Guingamp on Sunday.

After the Lyon match, they are at home to Le Havre on Saturday, which means their best players will have played three matches in a week before joining France's squad for a friendly against Turkey next Wednesday.
Maybe as a result of too many matches, PSG lost international keeper Bernard Lama last month and will now be without defensive midfielder Bruno N'Gotty for three weeks.
Lyon-born N'Gotty pulled a muscle in his right calf againt FC Vaduz in the European Cup Winners' Cup last Thursday and will miss a tie he had hoped to play against his former team mates.
PSG will also be without experienced defender Laurent Fournier against the young Lyon team, who won at Lens on Saturday and lie a flattering fifth in the table.
"It is a pity that all the absentees will be in defence," PSG assistant coach Joel Bats said. "Everybody can be replaced but we need everybody at the moment."
Lama, who has not conceded a goal since May 18, is proving difficult to replace. His stand-in, 21-year-old Vincent Fernandez, let in two goals in only his second first division match.
Fernandez was hardly to blame for either goal but Lama had played so well before his injury that some think he might have stopped one of them.
"We should not forget that Vincent saved us from conceding a third a couple of times," libero Alain Roche said.
The other highlight match on Wednesday evening pits champions Auxerre against Monaco, one of the few sides looking capable of matching PSG this season.

Auxerre welcome back marksman Lilian Laslandes for the tie whereas Monaco must to do without injured Eric Di Meco, Switzerland's Marco Grassi and Scot John Collins, who has been called up by his national side.

Bastia, doing unexpectedly well this season, are at home to Nantes in an intriguing clash at their Furiani stadium. Nantes, the 1995 champions, have not won a match since the start of the season and yet another loss could lead to major upheavals.
